[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Customer extensions need to provide React components that integrate seamlessly with core product UI. Without standardized component contracts, lifecycle management, and styling isolation, extensions create inconsistent user experiences, cause host application crashes, and impose unsustainable maintenance costs.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Define standardized React component extension contract including TypeScript props interfaces, lifecycle hooks, state management integration via context/Redux, styling isolation through CSS-in-JS, and error boundaries that enable customer extensions to integrate with core product UI while maintaining architectural boundaries and fault isolation.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

Apply this pattern when:
- Customer extensions require custom UI components within core product workflows (PTN-GOV-CUS-003 UI decision)
- Implementing UI injection points defined in PTN-APP-EXT-002
- Migrating ASP.NET server controls to React component extensions
- Building reusable UI extensions across multiple state implementations (>15 states)
- Full-stack or UI-only extensions per PTN-GOV-CUS-003 scorecard
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Seamless Integration**: Extension components behave like native product components (same props contract, same styling)
- **Isolation**: Extension failures don't crash host application (error boundaries contain failures)
- **Consistency**: Standardized contract ensures predictable behavior
- **Testability**: Clear component interface enables comprehensive testing (unit + integration tests)
- **Performance**: Optimized rendering through React memoization (<100ms render time)
- **Accessibility**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliance enforced through design system components

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Application Architect**: Defines React component extension contracts, error boundary strategies, and architectural boundaries for UI extensions.
- **.NET Developer**: Implements React component extensions following TypeScript props interfaces, CSS-in-JS isolation, and SDK integration patterns.
- **DDI Engineer**: Builds state-specific UI components that integrate with core product workflows using standardized extension contracts.
- **Platform Engineer**: Maintains the extensions SDK, design system packages, and Module Federation infrastructure.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

State-specific UI customizations enable states to tailor workflows to unique regulations. However, quality issues in UI extensions have caused customer escalations, highlighting the need for standardized component contracts.

**React and ASP.NET Extension Platforms**: Gainwell products have migrated to React 18 (ClaimsPro, MMIS Portal, ProviderConnect), while legacy ASP.NET applications remain. Extensions target both platforms, necessitating dual ASP.NET/.NET + React extension patterns.

**Design System Adoption**: Extensions using design system components achieve higher customer satisfaction than those using custom-styled components. This pattern drives design system adoption toward the target coverage level.

**Quality Incidents**: Production incidents caused by extension UI bugs (unhandled errors crashing host apps, styling conflicts, accessibility violations) have generated significant remediation costs and customer goodwill loss.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**React 18 Micro-Frontend Architecture**: Gainwell products use React 18 with Module Federation (Webpack 5), enabling runtime integration of customer extensions as federated modules. Host applications define extension points (PTN-APP-EXT-002); extensions register components implementing standard props interfaces.

**Extension SDK Package**: @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react (v2.4.0, 120KB) provides base types, error boundaries, context hooks, and testing utilities. Extensions that bypass the SDK create integration issues.

**Design System Package**: @gainwell/design-system-react provides 150+ components (Button, DataGrid, Card, Form inputs). Extensions must use design system for consistency; violations fail architecture review.

**TypeScript 4.9+ Required**: Extensions must provide TypeScript definitions for props interfaces. Enables compile-time validation of extension contracts, significantly reducing runtime errors.

**Bundle Size Constraint**: Each extension limited to <50KB gzipped. Host app installs 8-12 extensions simultaneously; total budget 600KB.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: Extension Errors Crashing Host Applications**
_Symptom_: Texas eligibility extension throws unhandled exception in useEffect; entire MMIS portal application crashes for all users.
_Root Cause_: No error boundary around extension component; error propagates to host React tree causing root unmount.
_Impact_: Extended outage, users affected across all tenants, significant incident resolution cost.

**Problem 2: Styling Conflicts Between Extensions and Host**
_Symptom_: Florida extension applies global CSS overriding host app styling; submit button disappears.
_Root Cause_: Extension uses plain CSS without scoping; class name collision with host styles.
_Impact_: Emergency hotfix required; 2-day deployment delay; customer escalation.

**Problem 3: Inconsistent Props Interfaces Across Extensions**
_Symptom_: California extension expects `userId` prop; host passes `user.id`; extension fails silently.
_Root Cause_: No standardized props contract; each extension team defines own interface.
_Impact_: Extended integration time; a significant portion of integrations require rework.

**Problem 4: Poor Performance from Unnecessary Re-Renders**
_Symptom_: Illinois extension re-renders entire DataGrid on every state change; UI freezes for 2-3 seconds.
_Root Cause_: Missing React.memo and useMemo optimizations; prop reference changes trigger renders.
_Impact_: User complaints about UI performance.

**Problem 5: Accessibility Violations in Extensions**
_Symptom_: Ohio extension custom dropdown not keyboard accessible; screen reader announces incorrectly.
_Root Cause_: Extension built custom component instead of design system; missed A11y requirements.
_Impact_: Section 508 audit failure; extended remediation; significant cost.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Competing Forces:**
- **Flexibility vs Consistency**: Extensions need freedom to implement unique state requirements, but consistency ensures quality user experience
- **Performance vs Features**: Rich UI features add bundle size; must balance under 50KB constraint
- **Isolation vs Integration**: Extensions must integrate seamlessly while remaining fault-isolated
- **Development Speed vs Quality**: Tight timelines pressure teams to bypass standards

**Hard Constraints:**
- **React 18+**: Extensions must use React 18 for concurrent features and Suspense
- **TypeScript Required**: Props interfaces must be TypeScript for compile-time validation
- **Design System Mandatory**: PTN-GOV-CUS-004 requires design system components; custom styling prohibited
- **Bundle Size <50KB**: Gzipped bundle size per extension cannot exceed 50KB
- **WCAG 2.2 AA**: All UI extensions must meet accessibility standards (automated + manual testing)
- **Error Boundaries Required**: Extensions must not crash host; error boundary mandatory
- **Browser Support**: IE11 (legacy contracts), Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari latest 2 versions

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

**Standardized React Component Extension Contract** defines typed props interfaces, lifecycle hooks, state management integration, styling isolation, and error boundaries. Extensions implement ExtensionComponentProps base interface, wrap components in ExtensionErrorBoundary, use design system components for styling, and integrate with host state via Redux or Context API.

**Key Principles:**
1. **Type Safety**: TypeScript props interfaces with strict typing enable compile-time validation
2. **Fault Isolation**: Error boundaries prevent extension failures from crashing host application
3. **Styling Isolation**: CSS-in-JS (styled-components/emotion) scopes styles to extension; no global CSS
4. **Design System First**: Extensions compose design system components; custom components prohibited
5. **Performance**: React.memo, useMemo, useCallback optimize rendering; code splitting reduces bundle size
6. **Accessibility**: Design system components ensure WCAG 2.2 AA compliance; automated testing enforced

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component   | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------ |
| **Extension Component** | React functional component implementing extension logic; receives props from host; renders UI using design system | React 18+, Design System, TypeScript |
| **Props Interface (ExtensionComponentProps)** | TypeScript interface defining contract between host and extension; includes `context` (tenant/user), `config` (extension settings), standard callbacks | @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react |
| **Error Boundary (ExtensionErrorBoundary)** | React error boundary wrapping extension component; catches errors, displays fallback UI, logs to telemetry; prevents host crash | React 18 Error Boundary API |
| **Theme Provider (DesignSystemThemeProvider)** | Provides design system theme tokens to extension; ensures consistent styling; supports tenant branding overrides | styled-components/emotion, @gainwell/design-system-react |
| **Extension Registry** | Runtime registry discovering and loading extension components; validates props interface compatibility; manages lifecycle | @gainwell/extensions-sdk-react, Module Federation |
| **State Integration Hooks (useExtensionContext)** | React hooks for accessing host state (Redux store, Context API); enables extensions to read/dispatch actions | react-redux, React Context API |

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**Extension Registration Flow:**
1. Extension registers component with Extension Registry at application startup
2. Registry validates TypeScript props interface matches ExtensionComponentProps
3. Extension loaded into memory but not rendered until extension point activated

**Runtime Rendering Flow:**
1. Host application renders ExtensionSlot component at extension point (e.g., claims detail page)
2. ExtensionSlot queries Extension Registry for registered extensions
3. For each extension, ExtensionSlot wraps component in ExtensionErrorBoundary
4. ExtensionSlot passes props (context, config) to extension component
5. Extension component renders UI using design system components
6. Extension subscribes to host state via useExtensionContext hook

**Error Handling Flow:**
1. Extension component throws unhandled exception (e.g., data fetch failure)
2. ExtensionErrorBoundary catches error in componentDidCatch lifecycle
3. Error logged to telemetry with stack trace and extension metadata
4. Fallback UI displayed in place of failed extension
5. Host application continues functioning; other extensions unaffected

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Isolated Extension (No State Sharing)**
Extension manages own state with useState/useReducer; no access to host state. Simplest approach; suitable for self-contained widgets (e.g., calculator, file uploader). Bundle size smallest (~30KB).

**Variation 2: Context-Based Integration**
Extension accesses host state via React Context API (useExtensionContext hook). Suitable for read-heavy extensions needing tenant context, user permissions. Moderate coupling; 40KB bundle.

**Variation 3: Redux Integration**
Extension dispatches Redux actions and selects from host store. Full bidirectional state integration. Highest coupling but enables complex workflows (e.g., claims adjudication). 50KB bundle.

**Variation 4: Micro-Frontend with Module Federation**
Extension packaged as Webpack Module Federation remote; lazy-loaded at runtime. Enables independent deployment and versioning. Adds complexity but supports large extensions (>50KB). See PTN-APP-EXT-013.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

1. **Use TypeScript for Type Safety**: 89% fewer runtime errors; enables IDE autocomplete and refactoring
2. **Implement Error Boundaries for Fault Isolation**: Mandatory per PTN-APP-EXT-001; prevents host crashes; logs telemetry
3. **Follow Design System Styling**: Mandatory per PTN-GOV-CUS-004; ensures consistent UX; automatic accessibility
4. **Use React Hooks for State and Lifecycle**: useState, useEffect, useMemo, useCallback simplify logic; avoid class components
5. **Implement Proper Loading and Error States**: Show spinner during async operations; display user-friendly error messages
6. **Optimize Bundle Size via Code Splitting**: Use React.lazy for large components; keep bundle <50KB gzipped
7. **Memoize Expensive Computations**: React.memo prevents unnecessary re-renders; useMemo caches calculations
8. **Validate Props with JSON Schema**: ExtensionManifest includes propsSchema; runtime validation catches contract mismatches
9. **Clean Up Side Effects in useEffect**: Return cleanup function; prevents memory leaks (subscriptions, timers, event listeners)
10. **Document Component Props and Behavior**: README with props table, usage examples, screenshots; Storybook stories

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

**Pitfall 1: Polluting Global Scope with Extension-Specific State**
**Symptom**: Extension sets `window.claimsCache = {...}`; causes conflict when multiple extensions access same global variable.
**Why**: Global state shared across host and all extensions; no isolation; namespace collisions.
**How to Avoid**: Use React Context, Redux, or module-scoped variables; never pollute window/global.
**Example**: Texas and California extensions both used `window.validationRules`; overwrite caused Texas logic to break; 2-day debugging.

**Pitfall 2: Missing Error Boundaries Causing Host Application Crashes**
**Symptom**: Extension throws unhandled exception; entire host application white screen; all users affected.
**Why**: React error propagates up component tree to root; unmounts entire app.
**How to Avoid**: Wrap all extensions in ExtensionErrorBoundary from SDK; log errors to telemetry; display fallback UI.
**Example**: Florida extension data fetch failure crashed MMIS portal; 3-hour outage; users unable to access the system.

**Pitfall 3: Inconsistent Styling Not Matching Design System**
**Symptom**: Extension button styled with Bootstrap CSS; doesn't match design system aesthetic; confuses users.
**Why**: Extension used custom CSS framework instead of design system; PTN-GOV-CUS-004 violation.
**How to Avoid**: Only use @gainwell/design-system-react components; no custom CSS; architecture review enforces.
**Example**: Ohio extension custom dropdown caused customer complaint; "looks broken"; 4-week rework to use design system Select component.

**Pitfall 4: Poor Performance Due to Unnecessary Re-Renders**
**Symptom**: Extension DataGrid lags when typing in filter input; entire grid re-renders on every keystroke.
**Why**: Component not wrapped in React.memo; props reference changes trigger render even when data unchanged.
**How to Avoid**: Use React.memo for components; useMemo for derived data; useCallback for event handlers passed as props.
**Example**: Illinois extension DataGrid (500 rows) re-rendered 12 times per second; UI froze; wrapped in React.memo and useMemo fixed.

**Pitfall 5: Insufficient Prop Validation Leading to Runtime Errors**
**Symptom**: Extension expects `userId` string; host passes `user.id` object; runtime error "Cannot read property 'length' of undefined".
**Why**: No runtime prop validation; TypeScript only validates at compile time; host app JavaScript bypasses types.
**How to Avoid**: Add JSON Schema propsSchema to ExtensionManifest; SDK validates at runtime; throw friendly error.
**Example**: California extension failed 32% of integrations; added propsSchema validation; caught mismatches at load time.

**Pitfall 6: Memory Leaks from Improper useEffect Cleanup**
**Symptom**: Extension subscribes to WebSocket in useEffect; doesn't close on unmount; memory usage grows 50MB per hour.
**Why**: Missing cleanup function in useEffect; subscription never canceled.
**How to Avoid**: Always return cleanup function from useEffect; unsubscribe, clear timers, remove event listeners.
**Example**: Texas extension EventSource subscription caused browser tab crash after 8 hours; added cleanup fixed.

### Real-World Example 1: Texas MMIS Eligibility Verification Widget

**Context**: Texas Medicaid (Texas Health and Human Services Commission) needed custom eligibility verification widget in MMIS portal claims detail page to validate member eligibility against state-specific rules not in core product.

**Implementation**:
- **Extension Point**: `claims-detail-panel` (defined in PTN-APP-EXT-002)
- **Props Contract**: `{ claimId: string, memberId: string, context: ExtensionContext }`
- **Component**: EligibilityVerificationWidget.tsx (42KB gzipped, React 18, TypeScript)
- **Design System**: Button, Card, Alert, DataTable from @gainwell/design-system-react-public (State-Exclusive IP → Public tier)
- **State Integration**: useExtensionContext hook accesses Redux store for member data
- **Validation**: JSON Schema propsSchema validates claimId/memberId at runtime
- **Error Boundary**: ExtensionErrorBoundary wraps component; fallback displays "Eligibility check unavailable"
- **Development Time**: 6 weeks (2 weeks design/dev, 2 weeks testing, 2 weeks accessibility audit)

**Outcome**:
- Integrated seamlessly with MMIS portal; users couldn't distinguish from native UI
- 4.5/5 developer satisfaction; "Easy to implement, great SDK documentation"
- WCAG 2.2 AA compliance (automated axe-core + manual testing)
- 0 host application crashes in 8 months production
- Significantly lower cost compared to implementing a full ASP.NET module
- Reused SDK and design system components; faster than previous Texas extension

### Real-World Example 2: California Provider Credentialing Status Dashboard

**Context**: California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) needed real-time provider credentialing status dashboard in ProviderConnect portal showing state-specific workflow stages.

**Implementation**:
- **Extension Point**: `provider-dashboard-widgets`
- **Props Contract**: `{ providerId: string, context: ExtensionContext }`
- **Component**: CredentialingStatusDashboard.tsx (48KB gzipped)
- **Design System Components**: Card, ProgressBar, Badge, Button, Modal
- **State Integration**: Redux integration; dispatches `fetchCredentialingStatus` action; selects from `providersSlice`
- **Performance**: React.memo wraps component; useMemo caches workflow stage computation; <100ms render
- **Accessibility**: Keyboard navigation; ARIA labels; focus management; screen reader tested
- **Development Time**: 8 weeks (3 weeks dev, 2 weeks integration testing, 2 weeks accessibility, 1 week security review for PHI access)

**Outcome**:
- 5/5 customer satisfaction; "Exactly what we needed"
- Accessed by 450 providers daily; 0 performance complaints
- 99.98% uptime; 2 incidents (both caught by error boundary, no host crashes)
- Delivered on time and within budget
- Enabled California to differentiate credentialing workflow vs other states

### Real-World Example 3: Florida Claims Batch Upload Progress Tracker

**Context**: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCFA) needed custom UI to track batch claims upload progress with state-specific validation feedback.

**Implementation**:
- **Extension Point**: `claims-batch-processing-panel`
- **Component**: BatchUploadProgressTracker.tsx (36KB gzipped)
- **Features**: Real-time progress bar, validation error list, retry failed claims button
- **WebSocket Integration**: useEffect subscribes to batch processing WebSocket; cleanup on unmount
- **Error Handling**: Error boundary with retry button in fallback UI
- **Testing**: 95% test coverage (Jest + React Testing Library); integration tests in host app

**Outcome**:
- Handles 10,000+ claims batches; real-time updates every 500ms
- Positive user feedback on batch processing visibility
- Memory leak fixed during QA (missing WebSocket cleanup); now stable
- 5-week delivery

### Before and After Comparison

**Before (Problem State):**
- No standardized React component contract; frequent integration failures requiring rework
- Missing error boundaries; host application crashes caused by unhandled extension errors
- Inconsistent styling; custom CSS leaked to host requiring hotfix remediation
- Poor accessibility; WCAG violations; Section 508 audit failures
- Low developer satisfaction; no consistent extension pattern to follow
- Significant development time spent debugging integration issues

**After (Solution State):**
- Standardized ExtensionComponentProps interface; integration failures reduced
- ExtensionErrorBoundary mandatory; host crashes isolated to extension-scoped error boundaries
- Design system components enforced; 0 styling conflicts; consistent UX
- WCAG 2.2 AA automated testing; accessibility compliance enforced at build time
- Improved developer satisfaction; standardized SDK reduces learning curve
- Integration debugging time significantly reduced

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-012-react-component-extension-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Customer extensions need React components that integrate seamlessly with core product UI, but without standardized contracts, extensions create inconsistent experiences and maintenance challenges.

**Solution:** Standardized React component extension contract with props interfaces, lifecycle hooks, state management integration, styling isolation, and error boundaries.

**When to Use:** Customer extensions requiring custom UI components, implementing UI injection points, migrating ASP.NET server controls to React, or building reusable UI extensions.

**Key Benefits:**
- Seamless integration with host application
- Fault isolation through error boundaries
- Predictable behavior through standardized contracts

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** React 18+, TypeScript 4.5+, design system npm package, extension SDK, Node.js 18+

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-EXT-002 (Extension Points), PTN-APP-EXT-013 (Module Federation), PTN-APP-EXT-017 (Design System Integration)
